\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ظاہر} (zāhir)}{ظاہر (zāhir)}]{\ur{ظاہر} (zāhir) — evident; plain}

\label{lesson:UR-C364-zahir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a nagging fear, then the Urdu for confidence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ظاہر}}
\textbf{\ur{ظاہر}} — \emph{zāhir} — \textquotedblleft{}evident; plain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{وہ} \ur{نہیں} \ur{آیا} \ur{تو} \ur{ظاہر} \ur{ہے} \ur{وہ} \ur{ناراض} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar voh nahīṅ āyā to zāhir hai voh nārāz hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If he has not come, he is clearly cross.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ظاہر}} (\emph{zāhir}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ẓāhir}, \textquotedblleft{}outward, apparent\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zāhir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zāhir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar voh nahīṅ āyā to zāhir hai voh nārāz hai.} — If he has not come, he is clearly cross.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a nagging fear, then the Urdu for confidence, then say \emph{zāhir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ظاہر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Evident; plain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لازمی} (lāzmī)}{لازمی (lāzmī)}]{\ur{لازمی} (lāzmī) — compulsory; bound to happen}

\label{lesson:UR-C364-lazmi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for confidence, then the Urdu for evident.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لازمی}}
\textbf{\ur{لازمی}} — \emph{lāzmī} — \textquotedblleft{}compulsory; bound to happen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{چلاتے} \ur{ہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{لائسنس} \ur{لازمی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp gāṛī chalāte haiṅ to lāisans lāzmī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you drive a car, a licence is compulsory.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لازمی}} (\emph{lāzmī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{lāzimī}, \textquotedblleft{}necessary\textquotedblright{}, built on Arabic \emph{lāzim}, \textquotedblleft{}binding\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lāzmī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āp gāṛī chalāte haiṅ to lāisans lāzmī hai.} — If you drive a car, a licence is compulsory.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for confidence, then the Urdu for evident, then say \emph{lāzmī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{واقعی} (vāqaī)}{واقعی (vāqaī)}]{\ur{واقعی} (vāqaī) — really; truly}

\label{lesson:UR-C364-vaqai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for evident, then the Urdu for compulsory.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{واقعی}}
\textbf{\ur{واقعی}} — \emph{vāqaī} — \textquotedblleft{}really; truly\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نمایاں} (numāyāṅ)}{نمایاں (numāyāṅ)}]{\ur{نمایاں} (numāyāṅ) — prominent; clearly visible}

\label{lesson:UR-C364-numayan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for compulsory, then the Urdu for really.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نمایاں}}
\textbf{\ur{نمایاں}} — \emph{numāyāṅ} — \textquotedblleft{}prominent; clearly visible\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{نشان} \ur{نمایاں} \ur{ہوتا} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{دیکھ} \ur{لیتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih nishān numāyāṅ hotā to maiṅ dekh letā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If this mark had stood out, I would have seen it.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نمایاں}} (\emph{numāyāṅ}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{numāyān}, \textquotedblleft{}appearing, visible\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ابھرنا} (ubharnā)}{ابھرنا (ubharnā)}]{\ur{ابھرنا} (ubharnā) — to emerge; to come to the surface}

\label{lesson:UR-C364-ubharna-emerge}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for really, then the Urdu for prominent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ابھرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ابھرنا}} — \emph{ubharnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to emerge; to come to the surface\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{کوئی} \ur{نیا} \ur{سوال} \ur{ابھرا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{بات} \ur{کریں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar koī nayā savāl ubharā to ham bāt kareṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If a new question comes up, we will talk.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{سوال} \ur{پھر} \ur{ابھرا}, \emph{voh savāl phir ubharā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ابھرنا}} (\emph{ubharnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ubharnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to rise, to swell\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{údbharati}, \textquotedblleft{}raises\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2038); \textbf{\ur{ابھارنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to bring out\textquotedblright{}, is its causative.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ubharnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar koī nayā savāl ubharā to ham bāt kareṅ ge.} — If a new question comes up, we will talk.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for really, then the Urdu for prominent, then say \emph{ubharnā} again
\end{itemize}
